unite_adi: REGULAR UPPER SECONDARY-YEAR 9-LEVEL: B1.1 - THEME 4: FAMILY LIFE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students prepare an interview, a poster/fact file, a short film etc. (paper or digital) about the jobs, work routines, work activities of their or their peers’ family members and present it to the class and receive feedback about it. The assignment will be evaluated by using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: It is generally accepted that people who start to learn a new language bring with them their pre-existing knowledge and transfer it to their new language learning. For instance, this theme is based on the concept of ''family members’ jobs, work routines, work activities and workplaces''. As students in year 9 (nine) of upper- secondary school, they are expected to know what a family member is, what a job is, what a work routine is, what a work activity is and what a workplace is in their own language. They are also aware of the fact that the majority of people in families have jobs, work routines, work activities, and workplaces. Students can think about and express such facts and situations in their own languages, but they may not know how to say them in a foreign language if they have not been covered at all or only partially covered in their existing curriculum. However, this existing knowledge in their own language would prepare them to identify the same concepts later and help them recognise, understand, and learn the new information about the new concept and theme more easily in their foreign language, English. In terms of preparation for the current new theme, it is assumed that the students have learnt some vocabulary items for ''some family members, jobs, work routines, work activities and workplaces such as ''father, mother, sister, brother, cousin, uncle, aunt, grandmother, grandfather, a doctor, a teacher, a police officer, a librarian an electrician etc.'' and ''a school, a hospital, an office, a garden, a farm etc''. It is also assumed that they have learnt how to ask and answer questions to introduce people very simply such as ''who is s/he? S/He’s/is my mother'' and to say their jobs such as ''What is her job? She’s/is a doctor'' by using grammatical structures that practise ''verb to be (am/is/are) in the Simple Present Tense in English from the previous themes or years. These vocabulary and grammatical structures are used as a basis by revising them and also expanding them for learning the new or additional vocabulary and grammatical structures and in the current theme by making the new grammatical items easier to learn.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is expected that students’ physical, cognitive, affective, social, and cultural factors are appropriate and suitable for learning about ''family members’ jobs, work routines, work activities and workplaces'' Recalling and practising basic vocabulary for ''family members, jobs, work routines, work activities and workplaces'' in English that they have learnt in the previous years would be helpful as a basis for moving on and learning the current content on the concept of ''family members’ jobs, work routines, work activities and workplaces''. Therefore, a dialogue chain game can be played where each student can ask a simple question about her/ his parents’ or some family members’ ''jobs, work routines, work activities and workplaces'' using the words s/he already knows (learnt in the previous years and revised at the beginning of the year) to the next student who answers the question and asks the same question to the next student, and so on, to revise all these vocabulary and grammatical structures from the previous themes in previous years by giving instructions in English as a preparation practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated to see how much they remember and how much they are able to understand and use the previously learnt vocabulary and grammar to build their competence in the current theme. It can be decided what to emphasise or practise in order to revise the previous knowledge and to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme.
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To help students discuss family members’ jobs, work routines, and workplaces in English through paired reading and question-asking by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Paired Jigsaw Reading – Family Jobs and Workplaces The teacher prepares a text that covers the jobs, work routines, and workplaces of different family members. The text is divided into two sections, each emphasising on two different jobs (e.g., a teacher and a mechanic, or a nurse and a chef). Students are paired up, and each student reads one section of the text independently. After reading, the students take turns asking each other questions about the jobs and workplaces they didn’t read about. For example, Student A might ask, ''Where does the mechanic work?'' or ''What are the nurse’s daily routines?''. This helps them complete their understanding of the entire text by filling in the missing information from their peer. At the end of the activity, each pair submits a completed worksheet that includes details about all jobs and workplaces covered in the text. The teacher evaluates how effectively students communicate and collaborate with their peers. S/he checks the correctness in answering questions and the completion of the worksheet for clarity, accuracy, and appropriate use of job-related vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To talk about family members’ jobs, work routines, and workplaces in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: TV Talk Show Role-Play - Family Jobs and Work Routines The classroom is set up like a TV talk show. One student acts as the host, while other students play the roles of different family members who are invited to the show to talk about their jobs and daily routines. The teacher prepares a list of different family members’ jobs (e.g., teacher, mechanic, nurse, chef) and puts them on small pieces of paper in a box. Each ''guest'' selects a job by drawing from the box. The host asks questions related to the family members’ jobs, work routines, and workplaces. Example questions include: ''What is your job, and what do you do every day? Where do you work? Can you describe your typical workday?''. The students in the roles of family members answer these questions, describing their jobs, work routines, and workplaces using job-related vocabulary and the present simple tense. The teacher evaluates students based on how well they answer the host’s questions, their use of target vocabulary, and the fluency and accuracy of their language. The teacher gives feedback on how well students maintain the conversation and use appropriate language related to family jobs and work routines. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To describe family members’ jobs and workplaces in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 1: Job and Workplace Pictionary The teacher writes job titles and workplace-related vocabulary (e.g., doctor, office, mechanic, factory) on small pieces of paper, folds them, and places them in a box. The class is divided into teams. One student from each team picks a piece of paper from the box and tries to explain the job or workplace by drawing it on the board, without speaking. The teammates must guess the job or workplace being drawn. Once they guess correctly, the team must use the job or workplace in a sentence describing a family member (e.g., ''My uncle is a doctor. He works at a hospital''). Points are awarded for each correct guess and a properly formed sentence. The team with the highest score at the end wins. The teacher assesses based on fluency, the number of correct guesses and sentences formed with accurate grammar and vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity. Objective: To describe family members’ jobs and workplaces in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar. Activity 2: Listening Practice - Daily Routines The teacher plays short audio clips that describe different people’s daily work routines, including details about their jobs and workplaces. Students listen carefully and complete a worksheet, where they must identify the job and workplace mentioned in each clip (e.g., ''He works as a teacher at a high school. He starts his day at 8 am.''). After listening, the class reviews the answers together. The teacher evaluates the students based on their skills to recognise key vocabulary and correctly identify the job and workplace in each listening task. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
